summary: In December 1984 a methyl isocyanate leak at Union Carbide's cost-cut, poorly maintained pesticide plant in Bhopal, India killed thousands overnight; the company dodged blame and left toxic waste that still poisons local groundwater.

evidence.note: 1976 union complaints about pollution open the negligence timeline
wage cuts, reduced training, worker killed by phosgene in 1981
unions campaign, leaders laid off, hunger strike and posters
refrigeration shutdown approved with US headquarters; West Virginia sister plant compared
gas release in the early hours of 3 December 1984, thousands die the first night
1985 act and later settlement with the Indian government
waste ponds leak into groundwater; abandoned chemicals left on site
2018 reporting on birth defects and illness in neighbouring slum
Dow buys Union Carbide in 2001 and disputes cleanup liability to the present

notes: Union Carbide is the bastard but the title frames the disaster, so the event is primary and the company secondary (no roles). Origin IN follows the event; the company is US-based. main_span runs from the 1976 safety complaints to the 1989 settlement (year from general knowledge; transcript just says eventually). Covered span ends 2019 with ongoing litigation and contamination.
